An Extreme Heat Warning is in effect through Wednesday, September 9, at 8 p.m. A Heat Advisory will go into effect Wednesday, September 9, at 8 p.m. to Thursday, September 10, at 8 p.m.
City of Irvine cooling centers are open to provide a safe, comfortable, and air-conditioned space for residents and their pets to beat the heat during the heat wave. All City of Irvine facilities are designated cooling centers where you can enjoy recreation programming or a good book while you cool off.
Heat Exposure
Prolonged exposure to excessive temperatures may cause serious heat-related illnesses such as heat exhaustion and heat stroke for those who are sensitive to heat. Symptoms of heat exhaustion may include heavy sweating, muscle cramps, weakness, headache, nausea or vomiting, and dizziness. Warning signs of heat stroke may include an extremely high body temperature; unconsciousness; confusion; hot and dry skin (no sweating); a rapid, strong pulse; and a throbbing headache. If symptoms of heat stroke occur, immediately call for medical assistance. Assist those with signs of heat stroke to a shady area and begin cooling their body with water.

articles.title: 2 firefighters suffer heat exhaustion in battle against Butler County grass fire, taken to ER - KWCH

articles.full_text:
BUTLER COUNTY, Kan. (KWCH) - A team effort in Butler County successfully knocked down a Labor Day Weekend grass fire near Towanda, but not without a medical emergency.
On its Facebook page, Towanda Fire Rescue reported that a couple of its firefighters needed emergency treatment for heat exhaustion after battling the fire Sunday afternoon, which “that spread into a large section of densely packed cedars and hedge.”
The fire rekindled and spread into a hay meadow. Besides the wind shift, the weather didn’t cooperate as the outside temperature in the area reached 107 degrees.
Towanda Fire Rescue reported that both firefighters were released after being treated for heat-related illness. The department also shared its appreciation for the mutual aid that kept the grass fire from spreading further.
On the call, crews from El Dorado, Benton, Potwin, Augusta, Andover and Whitewater assisted.

Keralam: Heat advisory issued as unusual September heat grips state
After the first week of September, Keralam has received only 5 mm of rainfall, just 7 per cent of the rainfall normally expected during this period
Keralam is witnessing an unusual weather pattern, with a weakening southwest monsoon coinciding with temperatures climbing well above normal across several parts of the state, with the mercury crossing 36 degrees Celsius at Punalur.
After the first week of September, Keralam has received only 5 mm of rainfall, just 7 per cent of the rainfall normally expected during this period. While Kasaragod and Kannur recorded relatively more rain, most districts received little significant rainfall.
Noticeable rise in daytime temperatures
The lack of rain has been accompanied by a noticeable rise in daytime temperatures. Data from weather stations across the state show temperatures 2 degrees Celsius to 4.4 degrees Celsius above normal at several locations.
Kottayam recorded the largest departure from normal, with a temperature of 35.2 degrees Celsius, 4.4 degrees Celsius above the normal 30.8 degrees Celsius. Punalur recorded the highest temperature among the stations listed, at 36.2 degrees Celsius, which was 4.3 degrees Celsius above its normal temperature.
Palakkad recorded 34 degrees Celsius, nearly 4 degrees Celsius above normal. At Kochi, the temperature touched 34.1 degrees Celsius, 3.4 degrees Celsius above normal. Thiruvananthapuram city recorded 33.8 degrees Celsius, 2.8 degrees Celsius above normal, while Vellanikkara also recorded 33.8 degrees Celsius, 3.7 degrees Celsius above normal.

Kannur airport recorded 33.7 degrees Celsius, while Kozhikode recorded 33 degrees Celsius, 2.3 degrees Celsius above normal. Kannur recorded 32.7 degrees Celsius, 2.1 degrees Celsius above normal. Karipur airport recorded 32.4 degrees Celsius, 2.6 degrees Celsius above normal.
At Thiruvananthapuram airport, the temperature was 32.3 degrees Celsius, 2 degrees Celsius above normal. The lowest temperature among the stations listed was recorded at the Naval station in Kochi, at 31.4 degrees Celsius, although this too was 1.3 degrees Celsius above normal.
Among the Lakshadweep stations, Amini recorded the highest maximum of 33.4 degrees Celsius, 3.4 degrees above normal. Minicoy recorded 33 degrees Celsius, while Agathi recorded 31.6 degrees Celsius.
Weakened monsoon
The temperature rise comes as the monsoon has weakened considerably. The resulting combination of poor rainfall and above-normal temperatures is creating conditions more typical of a dry spell than the early September weather usually expected in Kerala.

“High temperatures are likely to continue for another two to three days. Over the following two to three days, from September 10 onwards, there is a possibility of some rain, depending on the influence of the cyclonic circulation expected to form over the Bay of Bengal. The possibility of rain is higher in the central and southern districts," said Rajeevan Erikkulam, Meteorologist.
IMD issues precautions
The India Meteorological Department has also warned of temperatures 3 to 4 degrees Celsius above normal in Keralam from September 7 to 9. The State Disaster Management Authority has issued precautions, advising people to avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight, particularly between 11 am and 3 pm, and to remain adequately hydrated.
The authorities have also warned that the heat could increase the risk of heatstroke, sunstroke, and dehydration, apart from raising the possibility of fires in markets, buildings, and waste-disposal facilities. The risk of forest fires could also increase in areas adjoining forest regions.

At the same time, the weather pattern is not entirely dry. The IMD has forecast isolated heavy rainfall in some districts over the coming days and has issued Yellow Alerts for Alappuzha and Ernakulam on September 10, and Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, and Ernakulam on September 11.
The forecast points to a contrasting weather picture for Keralam with a weakening monsoon and rainfall deficit on one hand, and persistent above-normal heat on the other, with isolated spells of heavy rain still possible in parts of the state.

articles.full_text:
A heat advisory was issued Monday by the National Weather Service, warning of excessive temperatures in the middle of the week that could reach triple digits in interior areas.
On Tuesday the Bay Area Air Quality Management District issued a Spare the Air alert for Wednesday because of a forecast of unhealthy air quality due to high temperatures and light winds in the region. The advisory will be in effect from 10 a.m. Wednesday through 10 p.m. Thursday.
The air district said the weather conditions are expected to contribute to elevated levels of ozone, otherwise known as smog, particularly in the East Bay and South Bay. Ozone can cause health problems, particularly in children, older people and those with respiratory or heart conditions, according to the air district, which advises people to only exercise outdoors in the early morning hours on Spare the Air days.
Coastal highs are forecast to reach into the low 90s. Overnight lows will range from the mid 60s to mid 70s.
The high temperatures could cause heat-related illness in vulnerable populations if precautions are not taken, according to the Weather Service, which urged increased attention to hydration during the advisory.

The National Weather Service has issued a Heat Advisory for the Mother Lode, the entire San Joaquin Valley and the foothills of Mariposa County, from 10 AM Wednesday through 10 PM Thursday.
High temperatures ranging from 97 to 104 degrees are forecast, with the low temperatures mostly between 65 to 75 degrees.
This will equate to widespread Moderate HeatRisk, with areas of Major HeatRisk.
The hottest temperatures and areas of Major HeatRisk are expected to occur on Wednesday. The warmest overnight lows are expected in the Sierra foothills thermal belts and in urban areas. There will be little to no relief at night in areas of Major HeatRisk.
Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses, especially to anyone without effective cooling and/or adequate hydration.
Air conditioning is necessary; fans and open windows at night will not be enough. Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

articles.title: एक शीत मोर्चा आगे बढ़ रहा है; कल रात उत्तरी वियतनाम और उत्तर मध्य वियतनाम में तापमान में गिरावट आएगी, कुछ क्षेत्रों में तापमान 19 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे भी जा सकता है। - Vietnam.vn
articles.search_term: ("पारा चढ़ा" OR "पारा पहुंचा" OR तापमान OR "तापमान बढ़ा" OR "रिकॉर्ड तोड़ गर्मी" OR "डिग्री सेल्सियस" OR "पारा उबला" OR "अधिकतम तापमान" OR "तापमान 40 पार" OR "तापमान 45 पार" OR "तापमान बढ़ने की संभावना") Andaman and Nicobar Islands
articles.full_text:
शीत मोर्चे के प्रभाव के कारण, उत्तरी क्षेत्र में कुछ इलाकों में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है, और आज शाम (8 सितंबर) 7 बजे तापमान आमतौर पर 29-32 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा।
पूर्वानुमानों के अनुसार, 9 सितंबर की रात के आसपास, यह ठंडी हवा का झोंका उत्तरी वियतनाम के पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों, फिर पूर्वोत्तर के अन्य क्षेत्रों, उत्तर-पश्चिम के कुछ क्षेत्रों और उत्तरी मध्य वियतनाम को प्रभावित करेगा। ज़मीन पर, हवा की दिशा बदलकर उत्तर-पूर्वी हो जाएगी, जबकि तटीय क्षेत्रों में यह स्तर 2-3 पर और तटीय क्षेत्रों में स्तर 3 पर होगी।
वियतनाम के उत्तर-पूर्वी और उत्तर मध्य क्षेत्रों में 9 सितंबर की रात से मौसम ठंडा होने लगेगा। उत्तरी और उत्तर मध्य क्षेत्रों में इस शीतकाल के दौरान न्यूनतम तापमान आमतौर पर 21-24 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा, जबकि उत्तर के कुछ पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में तापमान 19 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे भी जा सकता है।
हनोई क्षेत्र में, 9 सितंबर की शाम से 10 सितंबर तक, बारिश, बौछारें और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, कुछ स्थानों पर स्थानीय रूप से भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है; 9 सितंबर की रात से मौसम ठंडा हो जाएगा।
समुद्र में, 9 सितंबर की रात से, टोंकिन की खाड़ी के उत्तरी भाग में हवा की दिशा बदलकर 4-5 तीव्रता की तेज़ उत्तरपूर्वी हवाएँ चलेंगी। 10 सितंबर की दोपहर और शाम से, टोंकिन की खाड़ी और उत्तर-पूर्वी सागर के उत्तरी भाग में 6 तीव्रता की तेज़ उत्तर-पूर्वी हवाएँ चलेंगी, जिनकी तीव्रता 7-8 तक पहुँच सकती है; समुद्री लहरें 1.5-2.5 मीटर ऊँची होंगी, और उत्तर-पूर्वी सागर के उत्तरी भाग में 2-3 मीटर ऊँची होंगी; समुद्र अशांत रहेगा।
9 सितंबर की शाम से 10 सितंबर तक उत्तरी क्षेत्र में हल्की बारिश, बौछारें और छिटपुट गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है, कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है। 10 सितंबर को उत्तर मध्य क्षेत्र में मध्यम से भारी बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है, कुछ क्षेत्रों में बहुत भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है। तूफान के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने, ओले पड़ने और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की प्रबल संभावना है।
मौसम विज्ञान एजेंसी ने चेतावनी दी है कि बवंडर, बिजली, ओलावृष्टि और तेज हवाओं के साथ आने वाले तूफान कृषि उत्पादन को प्रभावित कर सकते हैं, पेड़ों को गिरा सकते हैं, घरों, परिवहन बुनियादी ढांचे और अन्य सुविधाओं को नुकसान पहुंचा सकते हैं। साथ ही, विशेषज्ञों ने चेतावनी दी है कि भारी और स्थानीय स्तर पर भारी बारिश से छोटी नदियों और नालों में अचानक बाढ़ आ सकती है, ढलानों पर भूस्खलन हो सकता है और निचले इलाकों में जलभराव हो सकता है; तेज हवाएं और समुद्र में ऊंची लहरें जहाजों के आवागमन और अन्य गतिविधियों को प्रभावित कर सकती हैं।
